newsitem.title: USA: Forsyth County, Ga., sells first of new school GOs.
newsitem.headline: Forsyth County, Ga., sells first of new school GOs.

text.p: Georgia's Forsyth County will be the first to issue general obligation bonds for schools under a newly approved constitutional amendent authorizing a local option sales tax, finance director Dan Jones said.
The $48 million issue was being priced Tuesday via Knox, Wall & Co and will have maturities out to five years.
"We were trying to be first so we can take advantage of it before everybody else hits the market," Jones said.
Georgia voters approved an amendment in November allowing school districts to seek a one-cent local-option tax for up to five years to finance school construction and retire debt.
Previously, most Georgia school debt was repaid with property taxes.
Sixty-nine of the state's 180 school districts approved the taxes in referendums on March 18, the first opportunity for local voting.
Only four school districts rejected the tax hikes in March, and several others are planning referendums later in the year.
